objective.statement: Read and write the five notes that sit on the lines of the treble clef.
successCriteria: I can name any treble-clef line note without counting from the bottom every time.
I can place E, G, B, D or F on the correct line when asked.
I can explain why the treble clef is also called the G clef.

explanation.text: The treble clef is drawn so that its inner curl wraps around the second line up. That line is G — which is why the treble clef is also called the G clef.
Once you know G, the other lines follow by skipping a letter each time: the bottom line is E, then G, B, D and F at the top.
Make up your own sentence to remember E–G–B–D–F, for example 'Every Gorilla Buys Delicious Fruit'. Silly sentences are easier to remember!

explanation.caption: The five line notes of the treble clef, from the bottom line to the top.

music.textAlternative: A treble-clef stave with five semibreves rising from the bottom line to the top line, labelled E, G, B, D and F.
Three treble-clef notes: G on the second line, E on the bottom line and F on the top line, each linked to its key on the keyboard.

steps: The clef's curl highlights the second line; the G key lights up on the keyboard and sounds.
Move down one line (skipping the space) to the bottom line: E. The keyboard shows E just below G with F in between.
Jump to the top line: F. The keyboard shows that the top-line F is higher than the F in the bottom space.
The learner taps each line in turn and hears its note.
demonstration.textAlternative: Each step is also announced as text: clef curl → second line is G; bottom line is E; top line is F. Sound is optional.

guided.prompt: The clef curls around this line. What is the note?

music.textAlternative: A semibreve on the second line of a treble-clef stave.

hints: Which line does the curl of the treble clef wrap around?
It is the second line up — and the clef is named after it.

feedback.correct: Yes — G. The treble clef marks G on the second line.

mistakes.counted-from-top: Lines are counted from the bottom. This is the second line up, not the second line down.
mistakes.off-by-step: You're one step away. The curl of the clef points to this exact line: G.
mistakes.clef-confusion: In the bass clef this line would be B, but this stave has a treble clef.

feedback.fallback: This is G — the line the treble clef curls around.

guided.prompt: Start from G and skip up one letter to the next line. What is this note?

music.textAlternative: A semibreve on the middle (third) line of a treble-clef stave.

hints: G is the line below this one.
From one line to the next you skip a letter: G, (A), B.

feedback.correct: Right — B, on the middle line.

mistakes.line-space-swap: A is in the space just below. This note has the line running through it, so it's B.
mistakes.off-by-step: Count from G: G is the line below, the space is A, and this line is B.
mistakes.clef-confusion: In the bass clef the middle line is D. Check the clef: this is treble, so it's B.

feedback.fallback: It's B. Line notes skip a letter: G, then B.

music.textAlternative: A minim on the fourth line of a treble-clef stave, stem pointing down.

feedback.correct: Correct — D, on the fourth line.

mistakes.counted-from-top: Count lines from the bottom: this is the fourth line up, D.
mistakes.line-space-swap: C and E are in the spaces either side. The line runs through this note, so it's D.
mistakes.off-by-step: Count up the lines: E, G, B, D — this is the fourth.
mistakes.clef-confusion: That would be its name in the bass clef. In treble, the fourth line is D.

feedback.fallback: It's D: E, G, B, D, F from the bottom line up.

music.textAlternative: A crotchet on the bottom line of a treble-clef stave, stem pointing up.

feedback.correct: Correct — E, on the bottom line.

mistakes.counted-from-top: Counting from the top would give F. Always count from the bottom: this is the first line, E.
mistakes.off-by-step: One line up from E is G; this is the bottom line itself — E.
mistakes.clef-confusion: In the bass clef the bottom line is G. This is a treble clef, so it's E.

feedback.fallback: It's E — the bottom line of the treble clef.

independent.prompt: Put an F on a line of this treble-clef stave.

feedback.correct: Yes — the top line is F.

mistakes.line-space-swap: That F is in the bottom space. The question asks for an F on a line: the top line.
mistakes.wrong-octave: That's an F, but it's in a space. The only F on a line of the treble stave is the top line.
mistakes.clef-confusion: In the bass clef F is on the fourth line, but this is a treble clef.

feedback.fallback: The F on a line is the top line of the treble stave.

independent.prompt: Put a G on a line of the treble-clef stave.

feedback.correct: Correct — G on the second line, where the clef curls.

mistakes.line-space-swap: That's a space. G is on the second line — the one the clef curls around.
mistakes.counted-from-top: That's the second line from the top (D). Count from the bottom.
mistakes.wrong-octave: There is a G just above the stave, but it sits in a space, not on a line. The G on a line is the second line.

feedback.fallback: G is the second line up, marked by the treble clef's curl.

recap: The treble clef curls around G on the second line.
The line notes from the bottom are E, G, B, D, F.
Lines and spaces are always counted from the bottom.

mastery.completion: The lesson is complete when every step has been answered (with retries allowed). Only first-attempt, hint-free independent answers count as mastery evidence; guided steps never do.

provenance.authoredBy: Music Theory Path curriculum team (Brief 01 example)
provenance.notes: Original wording and examples. The mnemonic sentence is the author's own; learners are encouraged to invent their own. Book sections are recorded only as subject pointers.
